title.zh: 卷315 列傳一百二 高天喜 鄂实 三格 和起 唐喀禄 阿敏道 满福 豆斌 端济布 诺尔本
title.en: Volume 315 Biographies 102: Gao Tianxi, E Shi, San Ge, He Qi, Tang Kalu, A Min Dao, Man Fu, Dou Bin, Duan Ji Bu, Nuo Er Ben
title.raw: 卷315 列傳一百二 高天喜 鄂实 三格 和起 唐喀禄 阿敏道 满福 豆斌 端济布 诺尔本

sentences.zh: 列傳一百二

translations.literal: Biographies 102
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 102

sentences.zh: 高天喜鄂實三格和起唐喀祿阿敏道滿福

translations.literal: Gao Tianxi, E Shi, San Ge, He Qi, Tang Kalu, A Min Dao, Man Fu
translations.idiomatic: Gao Tianxi, E Shi, San Ge, He Qi, Tang Kalu, A Min Dao, Man Fu

sentences.zh: 豆斌端濟布諾爾本

translations.literal: Dou Bin, Duan Ji Bu, Nuo Er Ben
translations.idiomatic: Dou Bin, Duan Ji Bu, Nuo Er Ben

sentences.zh: 高天喜，甘肅西寧人。

translations.literal: Gao Tianxi was a native of Xining in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Tianxi was from Xining, Gansu.

sentences.zh: 天喜本準噶爾人，雍正中為我師所俘。

translations.literal: Tianxi was originally a Dzungar; in the Yongzheng reign he was captured by our army.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi was originally a Dzungar who had been taken prisoner by Qing forces in the Yongzheng era.

sentences.zh: 高氏撫為子，因從其族籍。

translations.literal: The Gao family adopted and raised him as a son, and he therefore followed their clan register.
translations.idiomatic: The Gao family adopted him as a son, and he was entered on their clan register.

sentences.zh: 從軍，累擢保寧堡守備。

translations.literal: He entered military service and was repeatedly promoted to garrison commander of Baoning Fort.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the army and rose step by step to garrison commander of Baoning Fort.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十二年，副將軍兆惠擊伊犁，天喜從參將邁斯漢赴援。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Qianlong, when Deputy General Zhaohui attacked Ili, Tianxi followed Major Maisihan to reinforce him.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 22, when Deputy General Zhaohui marched on Ili, Tianxi went with Major Maisihan to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 遇噶勒雜特賊百餘，擊殺之，獲其駝馬。

translations.literal: They met more than a hundred Galzat rebels, killed them, and seized their camels and horses.
translations.idiomatic: They encountered over a hundred Galzat rebels, defeated them, and captured their camels and horses.

sentences.zh: 既，聞兆惠被困濟爾哈朗，議馳救，邁斯漢怯不進。

translations.literal: Afterward, hearing that Zhaohui was trapped at Jierhalang, they discussed riding to the rescue, but Maisihan was too timid to advance.
translations.idiomatic: When they learned Zhaohui was besieged at Jierhalang, they debated a dash to relieve him, but Maisihan shrank from advancing.

sentences.zh: 巴里坤辦事大臣雅爾哈善以聞，上即奪邁斯漢官以命天喜。

translations.literal: Yarghasan, the commissioner at Barkol, reported this; the emperor at once stripped Maisihan of his post and gave the command to Tianxi.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Yarghasan at Barkol reported it; the emperor immediately removed Maisihan and put Tianxi in command.

sentences.zh: 尋遷金塔協副將。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to assistant deputy commander at Jinta.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made assistant deputy commander at Jinta.

sentences.zh: 再遷西寧鎮總兵，授領隊大臣。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to commander of the Xining garrison and appointed a column commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Xining garrison commander and made a column commander.

sentences.zh: 二十三年十月，師攻葉爾羌，兆惠議出間道襲取賊輜重，渡黑水。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twenty-third year, as the army attacked Yarkand, Zhaohui planned to take a bypath to seize the rebels’ baggage train and cross the Black River.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year 23, during the assault on Yarkand, Zhaohui proposed a flanking march to seize rebel supplies and cross the Black River.

sentences.zh: 天喜督兵修橋渡師，未及半，賊大至。

translations.literal: Tianxi supervised the troops in repairing a bridge for the army to cross; before half was done, the enemy arrived in force.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi directed men to build a bridge for the crossing; before it was half finished, the enemy came up in strength.

sentences.zh: 天喜聞兆惠陷賊陣，舍橋亟赴之，奮與賊戰，與鄂實、三格、特通額俱沒於陣。

translations.literal: Hearing that Zhaohui was trapped in the enemy formation, Tianxi abandoned the bridge and rushed to him, fought fiercely, and perished in battle together with E Shi, San Ge, and Tetunge.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Zhaohui was caught in the enemy line, Tianxi left the bridge and charged to his aid; he fought until he fell, along with E Shi, San Ge, and Tetunge.

sentences.zh: 上賦詩惜之。

translations.literal: The emperor composed a poem in lament.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote a poem mourning his death.

sentences.zh: 諡果義，又賜其家白金千。

translations.literal: He was posthumously titled Guoyi, and a thousand taels of silver were granted to his family.
translations.idiomatic: He received the posthumous name Guoyi, and his family was given a thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 鄂實，西林覺羅氏，滿洲鑲藍旗人，大學士鄂爾泰第二子。

translations.literal: E Shi, of the Xilin Gioro clan, was a man of the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner and the second son of Grand Secretary Ortai.
translations.idiomatic: E Shi of the Xilin Gioro clan, a Bordered Blue Banner Manchu, was Grand Secretary Ortai’s second son.

sentences.zh: 出為叔父鄂禮後。

translations.literal: He was made heir to his uncle E Li.
translations.idiomatic: He was adopted as heir to his uncle E Li.

sentences.zh: 自廕生授三等侍衛。

translations.literal: As a yinsheng he was appointed a third-rank bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: Through the yinsheng quota he received a third-rank bodyguard post.

sentences.zh: 累遷本旗副都統、左翼前鋒統領。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to deputy lieutenant-general of his banner and commander of the Left Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to deputy lieutenant-general of his banner and commander of the Left Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 兄鄂容安死阿睦爾撒納之亂，鄂實請從軍，授參贊大臣，佐定邊將軍成袞扎布，出西路。

translations.literal: When his elder brother E Rong’an died in the turmoil of Amursana, E Shi asked to take the field; he was made a consulting commissioner to assist the Pacification General Chenggezhabu on the western route.
translations.idiomatic: After his brother E Rong’an died in Amursana’s revolt, E Shi volunteered for service and was made consulting commissioner under Pacification General Chenggezhabu on the western front.

sentences.zh: 二十二年夏，成袞扎布令逐捕扎那噶爾布，鄂實以地險馬疲，中道引還。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twenty-second year, Chenggezhabu ordered pursuit of Zanagarbu; E Shi, citing difficult terrain and exhausted horses, turned the column back midway.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of year 22 Chenggezhabu ordered pursuit of Zanagarbu; citing rough country and spent horses, E Shi led the force back before the hunt was done.

sentences.zh: 上手詔詰責曰：「若謂地險，賊何以能行？

translations.literal: The emperor personally issued an edict of rebuke, saying: “If you say the ground is difficult, how can the rebels travel it?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him in an edict: “If the ground is too difficult for you, how do the rebels manage to cross it?

sentences.zh: 若謂馬疲，賊馬何獨能壯健？

translations.literal: If you say the horses are weary, why are the rebels’ horses alone strong and healthy?”
translations.idiomatic: If your horses are exhausted, why are the rebels’ mounts alone fresh and strong?”

sentences.zh: 」左授藍翎侍衛。

translations.literal: He was demoted to the left to a blue-plume bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to blue-plume bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 是冬，鄂實逐扎哈沁賊，斬一百四十餘級，獲牲械。

translations.literal: That winter E Shi pursued Zahakin rebels, beheaded more than a hundred and forty, and seized livestock and arms.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he pursued Zahakin rebels, killed more than 140, and took livestock and weapons.

sentences.zh: 上謂：「今當大雪，馬力應疲乏，尚能勦賊。

translations.literal: The emperor said: “Now there is heavy snow; horses ought to be weary, yet you can still destroy rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remarked: “Snow lies deep and horses should be spent, yet you still routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 彼時鄂實為參贊大臣，有事但諉諸將軍。

translations.literal: At that time E Shi was consulting commissioner and only shifted blame to the general whenever anything arose.
translations.idiomatic: When he was consulting commissioner, he had only pushed every difficulty onto the general.

sentences.zh: 茲以負罪，乃直前勦賊，朕知其隱矣。

translations.literal: Now, bearing guilt, he charges straight at the rebels—I know his motive.”
translations.idiomatic: Now, under a stain on his record, he leads the charge himself—I see through him.”

sentences.zh: 」量遷三等侍衛。

translations.literal: He was promoted in measure to third-rank bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised again to third-rank bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 死事，上令仍視前鋒統領賜卹，諡果壯。

translations.literal: He died in service; the emperor ordered condolence as for a vanguard commander and gave the posthumous name Guozhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in battle; the emperor granted funeral honors as for a vanguard commander and the name Guozhuang.

sentences.zh: 三格，棟鄂氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: San Ge, of the Donggo clan, was a man of the Manchu Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: San Ge of the Donggo clan was a Plain White Banner Manchu.

sentences.zh: 自諸生授藍翎侍衛。

translations.literal: From student status he was appointed a blue-plume bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service from student status as a blue-plume bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 累遷黑龍江副都統。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to deputy lieutenant-general of Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to deputy lieutenant-general of Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 命將索倫、巴爾呼兵三千，佐參贊大臣策楞出西路，為領隊大臣。

translations.literal: He was ordered to lead three thousand Solon and Barhu troops to assist Consulting Commissioner Celeng on the western route as column commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was told to lead three thousand Solon and Barhu soldiers under Consulting Commissioner Celeng on the western route as column commander.

sentences.zh: 策楞以怯懦逮，三格亦坐奪官。

translations.literal: Celeng was arrested for cowardice, and San Ge was also punished by loss of office.
translations.idiomatic: When Celeng was seized for cowardice, San Ge too was stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 旋复授正白旗蒙古副都統。

translations.literal: Soon he was again appointed Mongol deputy lieutenant-general of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reappointed Mongol deputy lieutenant-general of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 攻呼爾璊台吉賽音伯勒克等，再戰，掠其牧地，予三等輕車都尉世職。

translations.literal: Attacking the Khurun prince Sainberlek and others, he fought twice, raided their pastures, and was granted the hereditary office of third-class commandant of light chariots.
translations.idiomatic: In attacks on Khurun Prince Sainberlek and others he fought twice, overran their pastures, and received a hereditary third-class commandant of light chariots.

sentences.zh: 二十二年春，定邊將軍成袞扎布令逐捕扎那噶爾布，未得。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-second year the Pacification General Chenggezhabu ordered pursuit of Zanagarbu, but he was not taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year 22 Pacification General Chenggezhabu ordered Zanagarbu hunted down, without success.

sentences.zh: 秋，師至博羅和羅，遇叛黨額林沁達瓦等百餘戶，三格與戰。

translations.literal: In autumn the army reached Boluheluo and met more than a hundred households of the rebel Erinkindawa; San Ge engaged them.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, at Boluheluo, the column met over a hundred rebel households under Erinkindawa; San Ge gave battle.

sentences.zh: 會布魯古特台吉琿齊、呼爾璊台吉達瓦斬扎那噶爾布偽請降，並請招額林沁達瓦，三格信之，遽引師還，琿齊等旋遁去。

translations.literal: When the Burut prince Hunchi and the Khurun prince Dawa slew Zanagarbu and falsely asked to surrender, also asking to win over Erinkindawa, San Ge believed them and abruptly led the army back; Hunchi and the others soon fled.
translations.idiomatic: Burut Prince Hunchi and Khurun Prince Dawa killed Zanagarbu and feigned submission, asking also to bring in Erinkindawa; San Ge trusted them, withdrew at once, and Hunchi and his party soon escaped.

sentences.zh: 坐奪官，並削世職，以兵伍自效。

translations.literal: He was punished by loss of office and hereditary rank and served thereafter as a common soldier.
translations.idiomatic: He lost office and hereditary rank and served on as a private soldier.

sentences.zh: 死事，上命仍視副都統賜卹，諡剛勇。

translations.literal: He died in service; the emperor ordered condolence as for a deputy lieutenant-general and the posthumous name Gangyong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in battle; the emperor granted funeral honors as for a deputy lieutenant-general and the name Gangyong.

sentences.zh: 天喜、鄂實、三格並祀昭忠祠，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: Tianxi, E Shi, and San Ge were all enshrined in the Shrine of Loyalty and given the hereditary offices of commandant of cavalry and cloud-rider.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi, E Shi, and San Ge were all entered in the Shrine of Loyalty and granted hereditary commandant of cavalry with cloud-rider.

sentences.zh: 回部平，圖形紫光閣。

translations.literal: When the Muslim regions were pacified, their portraits were placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: After the Muslim regions were pacified, their likenesses were hung in the Hall of Purple Splendor.

sentences.zh: 特通額，策楞子也，附見策楞傳。

translations.literal: Tetunge was Celeng’s son; see the biography of Celeng.
translations.idiomatic: Tetunge was Celeng’s son; see Celeng’s biography.

sentences.zh: 和起，馬佳氏，滿洲鑲藍旗人。

translations.literal: He Qi, of the Majia clan, was a man of the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi of the Majia clan was a Bordered Blue Banner Manchu.

sentences.zh: 其先世阿音布，國初以軍功授拜他喇布勒哈番世職。

translations.literal: His ancestor Ayinbu, in the founding of the dynasty, received for military merit the hereditary rank of baitalabuleha fan.
translations.idiomatic: His forebear Ayinbu, in the dynasty’s early wars, won the hereditary rank of baitalabuleha fan.

sentences.zh: 和起襲職，授盛京協領。

translations.literal: He Qi inherited the office and was appointed assistant commandant at Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi succeeded to the rank and became assistant commandant at Mukden.

sentences.zh: 累擢寧夏副都統。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to deputy lieutenant-general of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to deputy lieutenant-general of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十九年，命與侍衛海福將千人佐定西將軍永常討達瓦齊，遷寧夏將軍。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Qianlong he was ordered, with Bodyguard Haifu, to lead a thousand men to assist the Pacification General of the West Yongchang against Dawachi, and was made commander of the Ningxia garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 19 he and Bodyguard Haifu were told to lead a thousand men under Pacification General of the West Yongchang against Dawachi; he was then made Ningxia garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 永常劾和起兵不及額，而和起先疏言將九百人以往，留百人護輜重，上得永常疏，不之罪也。

translations.literal: Yongchang impeached He Qi for not bringing the full quota of troops, but He Qi had earlier reported in a memorial that he would send nine hundred men forward and leave a hundred to guard the baggage train; when the emperor received Yongchang’s memorial he did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchang charged He Qi with shorting the troop quota, but He Qi had already written that he would advance nine hundred men and leave a hundred with the baggage; the emperor read Yongchang’s charge and did not blame him.

sentences.zh: 尋又命偕提督豆斌為巴里坤辦事大臣，策楞代永常為定西將軍，复劾和起送兵馬遲誤，當奪官，留任。

translations.literal: Soon he was again ordered, together with Provincial Commander Dou Bin, to serve as commissioner at Barkol; when Celeng replaced Yongchang as Pacification General of the West, he again impeached He Qi for delay in delivering troops and horses, which should have cost him his office, but he was kept in post.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon paired with Provincial Commander Dou Bin as commissioner at Barkol; when Celeng replaced Yongchang, he impeached He Qi again for late delivery of men and horses—a fault that should have meant dismissal—but He Qi was left in place.

sentences.zh: 旋复官，授欽差大臣關防，召詣京師諮軍事。

translations.literal: Shortly his rank was restored; he received the seal of imperial commissioner, and was summoned to the capital for consultation on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was soon restored; he received an imperial commissioner’s seal and was called to the capital for military consultation.

sentences.zh: 達什達瓦所屬宰桑訥默庫、曼集、烏達瑚們都等在軍私還游牧，命和起嚴鞫得實，以降人請予寬典，上不許，命正軍法。

translations.literal: The zaisang Nemuku, Manji, Udahu, and others under Dashidawa had privately returned to nomadizing while still with the army; He Qi was ordered to investigate strictly, established the facts, and though surrendered men asked leniency the emperor refused and ordered regular military law.
translations.idiomatic: Zaisang Nemuku, Manji, Udahu, and others of Dashidawa’s following had slipped away to pasture while nominally in service; He Qi was ordered to investigate, proved the case, and when surrendering tribesmen pleaded for mercy the emperor refused and commanded standard martial punishment.

sentences.zh: 二十一年十一月，輝特台吉巴雅爾叛，掠扎哈沁五百餘戶。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the twenty-first year the Khoyit prince Bayar rebelled and carried off more than five hundred Zahakin households.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of year 21 the Khoyit prince Bayar rebelled and seized more than five hundred Zahakin households.

sentences.zh: 定邊右副將軍兆惠令和起將索倫兵百人往按，檄吐魯番伯克莽阿里克等集闢展，而噶勒雜特宰桑哈薩克錫喇、布魯特台吉尼瑪陰應巴雅爾，詭以兵五百會。

translations.literal: The Right Deputy Pacification General Zhaohui ordered He Qi to lead a hundred Solon soldiers to investigate, and summoned the Turfan beg Mangalik and others to assemble at Bicheng; meanwhile the Galzat zaisang Hasak Sira and the Burut prince Nima secretly supported Bayar and falsely promised five hundred men to join.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Pacification General Zhaohui sent He Qi with a hundred Solon to look into it and called Turfan beg Mangalik and others to muster at Bicheng; meanwhile Galzat zaisang Hasak Sira and Burut prince Nima backed Bayar in secret and falsely offered five hundred men.

sentences.zh: 和起望兵至，疑之。

translations.literal: When He Qi saw troops approaching he grew suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: When He Qi saw soldiers approaching he became suspicious.

sentences.zh: 令莽阿里克诇之，紿告曰：「我兵也！

translations.literal: He ordered Mangalik to scout; they deceived him, reporting, “They are our troops!”
translations.idiomatic: He told Mangalik to reconnoiter; they lied to him, saying, “They are our men!”

sentences.zh: 」逾時，尼瑪等操戈前，莽阿里克自後譟，賊眾蜂集。

translations.literal: After a time Nima and the others advanced with weapons; Mangalik raised a clamor from behind, and the rebels swarmed in.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Nima and his party came forward armed; Mangalik shouted from the rear, and the enemy massed around them.

sentences.zh: 和起所將兵僅百人，負重創，手刃數賊，股中槍，徒步轉戰，至夜力盡。

translations.literal: He Qi had only a hundred men; badly wounded, he killed several rebels with his own hand, was shot in the thigh, and fought on foot until night, when his strength gave out.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi had only a hundred men; though gravely wounded he cut down several rebels himself, took a musket ball in the thigh, and fought on foot until night when he could fight no more.

sentences.zh: 和起垂死，命索倫侍衛努古德、彰金布突圍出，以所戴孔雀翎為識報兆惠，遂死之。

translations.literal: Dying, He Qi ordered the Solon bodyguards Nugude and Zhangjinbu to break out and report to Zhaohui, using the peacock feather he wore as a token; then he died.
translations.idiomatic: Near death he told Solon guards Nugude and Zhangjinbu to break out and reach Zhaohui, using the peacock plume he wore as proof; then he perished.

sentences.zh: 諡武烈，追封一​​等伯，以一等子世襲，祀賢良、昭忠二祠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously titled Wulie, posthumously ennobled as a first-class baron with inheritance as a first-class viscount, and enshrined in the Shrines of Worthies and of Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: He received the posthumous name Wulie, was raised after death to first-class baron with heirs as first-class viscount, and was honored in the Shrines of Worthies and of Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，師還，獲尼瑪及其子檻送京師，命戮於和起墓前。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, when the army returned, Nima and his son were captured in cages and sent to the capital; they were ordered executed before He Qi’s tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23, when the army came home, Nima and his son were taken in cages to the capital and ordered put to death before He Qi’s grave.

sentences.zh: 子和隆武，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Helongwu has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Helongwu has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 唐喀祿，他塔喇氏，蒙古正藍旗人。

translations.literal: Tang Kalu, of the Tatara clan, was a man of the Mongol Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Kalu of the Tatara clan was a Mongol of the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 自筆帖式再遷理籓院員外郎。

translations.literal: From clerk he was promoted again to an assistant director in the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from clerk to assistant director in the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十九年，賜副都統銜，命赴北路軍董理新降輝特台吉阿睦爾撒納、班珠爾等游牧地。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Qianlong he was granted the rank of deputy lieutenant-general and ordered to the northern army to oversee the pastures of the newly surrendered Khoyit princes Amursana and Banzhuer.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 19 he received deputy lieutenant-general rank and was sent to the northern front to manage pastures of the newly surrendered Khoyit princes Amursana and Banzhuer.

sentences.zh: 唐喀祿疏言：「班珠爾所屬多老稚不能耕，慮飢餒。

translations.literal: Tang Kalu memorialized: “Many of Banzhuer’s people are old or young and cannot farm; I fear hunger.”
translations.idiomatic: Tang Kalu wrote: “Many under Banzhuer are old or young and cannot farm; I fear they will starve.”

sentences.zh: 」上以距耕時尚遠，責其瑣屑，命撤還。

translations.literal: The emperor said the planting season was still far off, rebuked him for triviality, and ordered him recalled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said planting season was still distant, called the report petty, and ordered him back.

sentences.zh: 扎薩克林丕勒多爾濟初命同董理游牧，將軍別有指揮，唐喀祿疏請留。

translations.literal: The jasak Lin Pil Duoerji had first been ordered to oversee nomadizing together with him; the general had separate instructions, yet Tang Kalu memorialized asking to remain.
translations.idiomatic: Jasak Lin Pil Duoerji had been assigned with him to oversee nomadizing, but the general had other orders; Tang Kalu still asked to stay.

sentences.zh: 上責其不當，左遷理籓院筆帖式。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked him for impropriety and demoted him to clerk in the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked his presumption and demoted him to clerk in the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋复授員外郎，命送濟隆呼圖克圖自巴林赴伊犁，董理定邊右副將軍薩喇爾游牧。

translations.literal: Soon he was again made assistant director and ordered to escort the Jilong khutuktu from Baring to Ili and to oversee the pastures of the Right Deputy Pacification General Sarlar.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was assistant director again, told to escort the Jilong khutuktu from Baring to Ili and to manage pastures for Right Deputy Pacification General Sarlar.

sentences.zh: 复賜副都統銜，授領隊大臣，將駐防扎布堪兵千人，從定邊右副將軍哈達哈赴哈薩克，逐捕阿睦爾撒納。

translations.literal: He was again granted deputy lieutenant-general rank, made column commander, and led a thousand garrison troops from Zhabukan with Right Deputy Pacification General Hadaha into Kazakhstan in pursuit of Amursana.
translations.idiomatic: He received deputy lieutenant-general rank again, became column commander, and with Right Deputy Pacification General Hadaha led a thousand Zhabukan garrison troops into Kazakhstan after Amursana.

sentences.zh: 賊渠固爾班和卓遁入烏梁海，唐喀祿報哈達哈督兵擒之，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: The rebel chief Guerban Hezhuo fled into the Urianghai; Tang Kalu reported to Hadaha to lead troops and seize him, and was granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel chief Guerban Hezhuo fled into Urianghai country; Tang Kalu urged Hadaha to take him and was given a peacock plume.

sentences.zh: 阿睦爾撒納令其徒達瓦藏布入掠，唐喀祿令索倫總管鄂博什將五百人御之，降其眾三百。

translations.literal: Amursana sent his follower Davazangbu to raid; Tang Kalu ordered Solon commander Eboshi with five hundred men to meet them and induced three hundred of the enemy to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Amursana sent Davazangbu to plunder; Tang Kalu had Solon commander Eboshi meet them with five hundred men and brought three hundred of the enemy over.

sentences.zh: 尋命屯科布多。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to garrison Kobdo.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to hold Kobdo.

sentences.zh: 授理籓院侍郎、鑲藍旗蒙古副都統。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice-president of the Court of Colonial Affairs and Mongol deputy lieutenant-general of the Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice-president of the Court of Colonial Affairs and Mongol deputy lieutenant-general of the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 唐喀祿行按諸部，輝特降人屯紮克賽，每自相劫奪，請移屯呼倫貝爾、齊齊哈爾諸地；

translations.literal: Tang Kalu toured the tribes; Khoyit surrenderers were settled at Zakusai and constantly robbed one another; he asked that they be moved to Hulunbuir, Qiqihar, and other places;
translations.idiomatic: On inspection Tang Kalu found Khoyit surrenderers at Zakusai constantly raiding one another and asked to move them to Hulunbuir, Qiqihar, and elsewhere;

sentences.zh: 喀爾喀俘獲扎哈沁、特楞古特、奇爾吉斯、烏爾罕濟蘭諸部人萬餘，請以扎哈沁人移駐卡倫內；

translations.literal: the Khalkha had captured more than ten thousand people of the Zahakin, Terengut, Kirghiz, and Uryan Jilan tribes; he asked that the Zahakin be moved inside the border posts;
translations.idiomatic: Khalkha captives from Zahakin, Terengut, Kirghiz, and Uryan Jilan numbered over ten thousand; he asked to station Zahakin people inside the border posts;

sentences.zh: 特楞古特、奇爾吉斯、烏爾罕濟蘭人給東三省兵丁為奴；

translations.literal: Terengut, Kirghiz, and Uryan Jilan people were to be given as slaves to troops in the Three Eastern Provinces;
translations.idiomatic: Terengut, Kirghiz, and Uryan Jilan captives were to be assigned as slaves to troops in the Three Eastern Provinces;

sentences.zh: 杜爾伯特游牧請移烏蘭固木：上並從其請。

translations.literal: the Durbot asked to move their pastures to Ulan Gumu: the emperor granted all these requests.
translations.idiomatic: the Durbot asked to move their pastures to Ulan Gumu: the emperor approved every request.

sentences.zh: 師出西路擊哈薩克錫喇，命唐喀祿屯額爾齊斯為聲援。

translations.literal: When the army marched on the western route against the Kazakh Sira, Tang Kalu was ordered to hold the Irtysh as support.
translations.idiomatic: As columns on the western route struck the Kazakh Sira, Tang Kalu was told to hold the Irtysh in support.

sentences.zh: 阿睦爾撒納敗走，唐喀祿诇知杜爾伯特貝勒巴圖博羅特、台吉阿喇善等潛與相結；

translations.literal: After Amursana was defeated and fled, Tang Kalu learned that Durbot beile Batubolot, taiji Alashan, and others were secretly in contact with him;
translations.idiomatic: When Amursana fled in defeat, Tang Kalu learned that Durbot Beile Batubolot, Taiji Alashan, and others were secretly in league with him;

sentences.zh: 遣兵攻之輝巴朗山，擒阿喇善等，並戮烏梁海五十餘戶，遂赴塔爾巴哈台逐捕阿睦爾撒納及哈薩克錫喇，賜御用荷包、鼻煙壺。

translations.literal: he sent troops to attack them at Huibolang Mountain, captured Alashan and others, and executed more than fifty Urianghai households; then he went to Tarbagatai in pursuit of Amursana and the Kazakh Sira, and was granted an imperial purse and snuff bottle.
translations.idiomatic: he sent troops against them at Huibolang Mountain, took Alashan and others, put more than fifty Urianghai households to death, then marched to Tarbagatai after Amursana and Kazakh Sira and received an imperial purse and snuff bottle.

sentences.zh: 師至塔爾巴哈台，糧罄馬乏，唐喀祿引師退，疏言遵旨撤兵，上怒，左授藍翎侍衛，佐定邊左副將軍納穆扎爾出北路。

translations.literal: When the army reached Tarbagatai, grain and horses were exhausted; Tang Kalu led the troops back and reported in a memorial that he was withdrawing on orders; the emperor was angry and demoted him to blue-plume bodyguard to assist Left Deputy Pacification General Namuzha’er on the northern route.
translations.idiomatic: At Tarbagatai supplies and horses gave out; Tang Kalu withdrew and wrote that he was obeying orders to pull back; the emperor was furious, demoted him to blue-plume bodyguard, and set him under Left Deputy Pacification General Namuzha’er on the northern route.

sentences.zh: 降人和碩齊，上擢用至散秩大臣，至是令護哈薩克來使入邊，上命納穆扎爾遣唐喀祿將二百人迎之。

translations.literal: The surrendered Hoshochi had been promoted to honorary grand minister; now he was ordered to escort a Kazakh envoy into the border; the emperor commanded Namuzha’er to send Tang Kalu with two hundred men to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: The surrendered Hoshochi, raised to honorary grand minister, was now to escort a Kazakh envoy inward; the emperor told Namuzha’er to send Tang Kalu with two hundred men to receive them.

sentences.zh: 阿睦爾撒納竄俄羅斯，上命唐喀祿偕和碩齊駐額爾齊斯偵禦。

translations.literal: Amursana fled into Russia; the emperor ordered Tang Kalu, together with Hoshochi, to garrison the Irtysh on watch.
translations.idiomatic: Amursana slipped into Russia; the emperor ordered Tang Kalu and Hoshochi to hold the Irtysh on guard.

sentences.zh: 二十三年三月，土爾扈特舍棱等謀走俄羅斯，上命偕和碩齊逐捕。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-third year, when the Torghut Shereng and others plotted flight to Russia, the emperor ordered him to pursue together with Hoshochi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 23, when Torghut Shereng and others plotted escape to Russia, he was ordered to hunt them down with Hoshochi.

sentences.zh: 四月，師次佈固圖河，獲舍棱弟勞章扎卜。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the army halted at Bugutu River and captured Shereng’s younger brother Lao Zhangzhabu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the column camped on the Bugutu River and took Shereng’s brother Lao Zhangzhabu.

sentences.zh: 勞章扎卜詭為兄乞降，唐喀祿未敢信，和碩齊遽縱之還。

translations.literal: Lao Zhangzhabu falsely pleaded surrender for his brother; Tang Kalu did not dare trust him, but Hoshochi at once let him go back.
translations.idiomatic: Lao Zhangzhabu feigned surrender for his brother; Tang Kalu would not trust him, but Hoshochi immediately sent him back.

sentences.zh: 越日，舍棱詭約降，獻酒，和碩齊飲之，邀唐喀祿過其營，賊噪而起。

translations.literal: The next day Shereng falsely promised surrender and offered wine; Hoshochi drank it and invited Tang Kalu to his camp; the rebels rose shouting.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Shereng again feigned submission and offered wine; Hoshochi drank and invited Tang Kalu into camp; the rebels sprang up with a shout.

sentences.zh: 唐喀祿及侍衛富錫爾、穆倫保、佛爾慶額力戰，均遇害，和碩齊更衣降。

translations.literal: Tang Kalu and the bodyguards Fuxi’er, Mulunbao, and Fo’erqing’e fought hard and were all killed; Hoshochi changed clothes and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Kalu and bodyguards Fuxi’er, Mulunbao, and Fo’erqing’e fought until they were slain; Hoshochi changed clothes and submitted.

sentences.zh: 事聞，賜騎都尉世職，祀昭忠祠。

translations.literal: When word came, he was granted the hereditary office of commandant of cavalry and enshrined in the Shrine of Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: On report of his death he received a hereditary commandant of cavalry and a place in the Shrine of Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 富錫爾、佛爾慶額，皆滿洲鑲黃旗人；

translations.literal: Fuxi’er and Fo’erqing’e were both men of the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner;
translations.idiomatic: Fuxi’er and Fo’erqing’e were both Bordered Yellow Banner Manchus;

sentences.zh: 穆倫保，滿洲正白旗人：皆賜雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: Mulunbao was a man of the Manchu Plain White Banner: all were granted the hereditary office of cloud-rider.
translations.idiomatic: Mulunbao was a Plain White Banner Manchu: all received hereditary cloud-rider rank.

sentences.zh: 阿敏道，圖爾格期氏，蒙古鑲紅旗人，世居察哈爾。

translations.literal: A Min Dao, of the Turgut clan, was a man of the Mongol Bordered Red Banner, long resident in Chahar.
translations.idiomatic: A Min Dao of the Turgut clan was a Bordered Red Banner Mongol whose family had long lived in Chahar.

sentences.zh: 父阿吉斯，康熙間討噶爾丹，以員外郎從軍，中道糧匱，兵苦飢。

translations.literal: His father Ajisi, in the Kangxi reign when campaigning against Galdan, followed the army as an assistant director; midway provisions failed and the troops suffered hunger.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ajisi, in the Kangxi wars against Galdan, went as an assistant director; on the march grain ran out and the soldiers starved.

sentences.zh: 阿吉斯言於眾曰：「我等官兵世受國恩，甘斃道路。

translations.literal: Ajisi said to the troops: “We officers and soldiers have received the state’s grace for generations; we are willing to die on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Ajisi told the men: “We have eaten the dynasty’s bread for generations; we are ready to die on the march.

sentences.zh: 誓竭力前進。

translations.literal: We swear to press forward with all our strength.”
translations.idiomatic: We swear to drive forward with all our might.”

sentences.zh: 」眾皆諾。

translations.literal: All assented.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是有昭莫多之勝。

translations.literal: Thus came the victory at Jao Modo.
translations.idiomatic: That is how the victory at Jao Modo was won.

sentences.zh: 聖祖嘉其能，予拖沙喇哈番世職。

translations.literal: The Sacred Ancestor praised his ability and granted the hereditary rank of tuoshalaha fan.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi praised his spirit and gave him the hereditary rank of tuoshalaha fan.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 阿敏道，襲職。

translations.literal: A Min Dao inherited the office.
translations.idiomatic: A Min Dao succeeded to the rank.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，累遷二等侍衛。

translations.literal: In the early Yongzheng reign he was repeatedly promoted to second-rank bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongzheng he rose to second-rank bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 九年，命將巴里呼兵百人自固爾班塞堪赴巴爾坤佐軍，又命偕侍讀學士查克丹調喀爾喀兵三千率之往。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was ordered to lead a hundred Barhu troops from Guerban Saikan to Barkol to assist the army, and again ordered, together with Reader of the Hanlin Academy Chakedan, to muster three thousand Khalkha troops and lead them thither.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he was told to lead a hundred Barhu soldiers from Guerban Saikan to Barkol and, with Hanlin Reader Chakedan, to raise three thousand Khalkha troops and march them there.

sentences.zh: 尋复偕護軍統領費雅思哈赴烏爾輝音扎罕練兵。

translations.literal: Soon he was again ordered, together with Guard Commander Feiyasaha, to go to Wuerhui Yinzahan to drill troops.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent with Guard Commander Feiyasaha to Wuerhui Yinzahan to train troops.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，準噶爾乞和，撤軍，阿敏道還京，授鑲藍旗察哈爾總管。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong the Dzungars sued for peace, the army was withdrawn, and A Min Dao returned to the capital and was appointed Chahar commander of the Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 the Dzungars sued for peace, the army came home, and A Min Dao was made Chahar commander of the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 十九年，師收烏梁海，將察哈爾兵以從，加副都統銜。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, when the army recovered the Urianghai, he led Chahar troops in the campaign and was given the rank of deputy lieutenant-general.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19, during the recovery of Urianghai, he led Chahar troops and received deputy lieutenant-general rank.

sentences.zh: 二十年，遷所獲巴爾沁人等於齊拉罕。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he moved captured Barjin people to Qilahan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 he resettled captured Barjin people at Qilahan.

sentences.zh: 師定伊犁，定北將軍班第奏以阿敏道督台站。

translations.literal: When the army pacified Ili, the Pacification General of the North Bandi memorialized that A Min Dao should supervise the courier stations.
translations.idiomatic: After Ili was secured, Northern Pacification General Bandi asked that A Min Dao oversee the courier stations.

sentences.zh: 是年，阿睦爾撒納叛，班第陷賊。

translations.literal: That year Amursana rebelled and Bandi fell into the rebels’ hands.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Amursana rebelled and Bandi was trapped among the enemy.

sentences.zh: 阿巴噶斯、哈丹附逆肆掠，台站中斷。

translations.literal: Abagasi and Hadan joined the revolt and plundered wildly; the courier lines were cut.
translations.idiomatic: Abagasi and Hadan sided with the rebels and ravaged the routes until the stations were severed.

sentences.zh: 阿敏道輒督兵巡徼，使驛遞恆得相續。

translations.literal: A Min Dao repeatedly led troops on patrol so that the post relays could always be kept up.
translations.idiomatic: A Min Dao patrolled again and again so the post relays never quite failed.

sentences.zh: 會定西將軍永常自木壘退駐烏爾圖布拉克，撤阿敏道還。

translations.literal: When Pacification General of the West Yongchang withdrew from Mulei to station at Wuer Tubulake, A Min Dao was also withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: When Western Pacification General Yongchang fell back from Mulei to Wuer Tubulake, A Min Dao was pulled back as well.

sentences.zh: 上奪永常官，以策楞代將。

translations.literal: The emperor stripped Yongchang of office and replaced him with Celeng as commander.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor removed Yongchang and put Celeng in command.

sentences.zh: 命阿敏道將精騎詣伊犁求班第消息。

translations.literal: A Min Dao was ordered to lead picked cavalry to Ili to seek news of Bandi.
translations.idiomatic: A Min Dao was told to take elite horsemen to Ili for word of Bandi.

sentences.zh: 策楞不即遣，上詰責之。

translations.literal: Celeng did not send him at once; the emperor rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Celeng delayed sending him; the emperor scolded him.

sentences.zh: 尋將千人捕阿巴噶斯、哈丹賊眾。

translations.literal: Soon he led a thousand men to capture the rebel bands of Abagasi and Hadan.
translations.idiomatic: He soon led a thousand men against the bands of Abagasi and Hadan.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，授鑲藍旗蒙古副都統。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was appointed Mongol deputy lieutenant-general of the Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21 he became Mongol deputy lieutenant-general of the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 時回酋布拉呢敦、霍集占有異志，定邊右副將軍兆惠诇知之，遣阿敏道將索倫兵百、厄魯特兵三千赴葉爾羌、喀什噶爾慰撫，且使致二渠。

translations.literal: At that time the Muslim chiefs Burhanuddin and Khojaji harbored disloyal designs; Right Deputy Pacification General Zhaohui learned of it and sent A Min Dao with a hundred Solon soldiers and three thousand Olot troops to Yarkand and Kashgar to reassure the people and also to summon the two chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: The Muslim leaders Burhanuddin and Khojaji were turning disloyal; Zhaohui learned of it and sent A Min Dao with a hundred Solon and three thousand Olot troops to Yarkand and Kashgar to reassure the people and summon the two chiefs.

sentences.zh: 至庫車，霍集占佈在焉，閉城拒我師。

translations.literal: At Kucha, Khojaji was present and closed the city against our army.
translations.idiomatic: At Kucha, Khojaji was inside and shut the gates on the column.

sentences.zh: 阿敏道斬遊騎四十餘，圍之。

translations.literal: A Min Dao cut down more than forty mounted scouts and besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: A Min Dao killed more than forty mounted scouts and invested the town.

sentences.zh: 城人詭言曰：「厄魯特吾仇，慮為害。

translations.literal: The townspeople deceived them, saying: “The Olot are our enemies; we fear harm from them.
translations.idiomatic: The townspeople lied: “The Olot are our enemies; we fear they will hurt us.

sentences.zh: 撤還即納降。

translations.literal: Withdraw them and we will submit at once.”
translations.idiomatic: Send them away and we will surrender at once.”

sentences.zh: 」阿敏道遂命厄魯特兵退，僅留索倫兵百。

translations.literal: A Min Dao therefore ordered the Olot troops to withdraw, leaving only a hundred Solon soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: A Min Dao ordered the Olot back, keeping only a hundred Solon.

sentences.zh: 或慮有變，阿敏道曰：「吾招撫回眾，惟期於國有濟，何暇他慮？

translations.literal: Some feared treachery; A Min Dao said: “I am winning over the Muslim people and care only that the state may benefit—what leisure have I for other worries?
translations.idiomatic: Some warned of a trap; A Min Dao said: “I am winning the Muslims over for the state’s good—why should I fret about anything else?

sentences.zh: 」遂入，為霍集占所執。

translations.literal: He then entered and was seized by Khojaji.
translations.idiomatic: He went in and Khojaji took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，上諭諸將檄霍集占送阿敏道還，不從，謀加害。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year the emperor instructed the generals in a proclamation to Khojaji to return A Min Dao; he refused and plotted harm.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22 the emperor told the generals to demand A Min Dao back in a proclamation to Khojaji; Khojaji refused and plotted his death.

sentences.zh: 庫車伯克呼岱巴爾以告，阿敏道謀脫歸，不克，死之。

translations.literal: The Kucha beg Hudai Baer informed him; A Min Dao tried to escape but could not and died.
translations.idiomatic: Kucha beg Hudai Baer warned him; A Min Dao tried to break out, failed, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 二等男署察哈爾營總旺扎勒及諸裨將繃科、耨金吹、扎木蘇

translations.literal: The acting Chahar camp commander of the second-class baron Wangzhale and the lieutenants Bengke, Noujinchui, and Zhamusu
translations.idiomatic: Acting Chahar commander Wangzhale, a second-class baron, and lieutenants Bengke, Noujinchui, and Zhamusu

sentences.zh: 七、巴克薩拾，並索倫兵百人，皆從死。

translations.literal: seven men including Baksa Shi, together with a hundred Solon soldiers, all died with him.
translations.idiomatic: seven others including Baksa Shi, and a hundred Solon soldiers, all died with him.

sentences.zh: 事平，諸有功者圖形紫光閣，阿敏道列後五十功臣，加世職為騎都尉兼一云騎尉，祀昭忠祠。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, meritorious men were portrayed in the Hall of Purple Splendor; A Min Dao was listed among the fifty later meritorious subjects, his hereditary rank was raised to commandant of cavalry with one cloud-rider, and he was enshrined in the Shrine of Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: After the region was pacified, heroes were painted in the Hall of Purple Splendor; A Min Dao was ranked among the fifty later honorees, raised to commandant of cavalry with one cloud-rider, and placed in the Shrine of Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 旺札勒加雲騎尉，繃科等皆予雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: Wangzhale received an added cloud-rider; Bengke and the others were all granted hereditary cloud-rider rank.
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhale gained an added cloud-rider; Bengke and the rest received hereditary cloud-rider rank.

sentences.zh: 滿福，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲鑲藍旗人。

translations.literal: Man Fu, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a man of the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Man Fu of the Guwalgiya clan was a Bordered Blue Banner Manchu.

sentences.zh: 自世管佐領累擢拉林副都統。

translations.literal: From hereditary assistant commandant he was repeatedly promoted to deputy lieutenant-general of Lalin.
translations.idiomatic: From hereditary assistant commandant he rose to deputy lieutenant-general of Lalin.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十二年，遷都統，駐巴里坤。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Qianlong he was made lieutenant-general and stationed at Barkol.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 22 he became lieutenant-general at Barkol.

sentences.zh: 命將吉林兵千人屯吐魯番，尋授領隊大臣。

translations.literal: He was ordered to lead a thousand Jilin troops to garrison Turfan and soon was made column commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was told to garrison Turfan with a thousand Jilin troops and soon made column commander.

sentences.zh: 定邊將軍成袞扎佈出珠勒都斯，令滿福將三百人巡視阿勒輝至烏納哈特十三台站，搜剿嗎哈沁。

translations.literal: When Pacification General Chenggezhabu marched from Zhuledusi, Man Fu was ordered with three hundred men to patrol the thirteen courier stations from Alehui to Wunahate and to search out and destroy mahajin.
translations.idiomatic: When Pacification General Chenggezhabu moved from Zhuledusi, Man Fu patrolled thirteen stations from Alehui to Wunahate with three hundred men and hunted mahajin.

sentences.zh: 沙拉斯、嗎唬斯既降复叛，掠台站，上命滿福自阿勒輝往剿，又令巴里坤辦事大臣阿里袞帥師與會。

translations.literal: Shalasi and Mahusi had surrendered and rebelled again, plundering the stations; the emperor ordered Man Fu to campaign from Alehui, and also ordered Commissioner Alihun to lead an army to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Shalasi and Mahusi had submitted, rebelled again, and raided the posts; the emperor ordered Man Fu out from Alehui and Commissioner Alihun to bring a column to meet him.

sentences.zh: 阿里袞未至，滿福師次肯色嶺，與賊遇，擊之，賊敗走，偽遣人乞降，且言賊渠已就縛，請除道迎。

translations.literal: Before Alihun arrived, Man Fu’s army camped at Kense Ridge and met the enemy; he attacked and the enemy fled, falsely sending men to beg surrender and saying the rebel chiefs were already bound, asking that the road be cleared to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Aliahun had not come up when Man Fu met the enemy at Kense Ridge, routed them, and received false envoys claiming the chiefs were bound and begging him to clear the road.

sentences.zh: 滿福信之，行次哈喇和落，徑險林密，下臨深溝。

translations.literal: Man Fu believed them; marching to Halaluhe, the route ran through dense forest above a deep ravine.
translations.idiomatic: Man Fu trusted them; at Halaluhe the path plunged through thick woods above a deep gorge.

sentences.zh: 滿福悟為賊所紿，急麾前隊返。

translations.literal: Man Fu realized he had been deceived by the rebels and urgently ordered the vanguard to turn back.
translations.idiomatic: He saw the trap and ordered the van to wheel about.

sentences.zh: 賊千餘突自林中出，圍我師。

translations.literal: More than a thousand rebels burst from the woods and surrounded our army.
translations.idiomatic: Over a thousand rebels rushed from the trees and ringed the column.

sentences.zh: 滿福厲聲督兵力戰，被創墜溝，死之。

translations.literal: Man Fu shouted orders and fought fiercely; he was wounded, fell into the ravine, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Man Fu roared them on, was struck, fell into the gorge, and died.

sentences.zh: 上以滿福雖為賊所愚，愍其捐軀，命如陣亡例議卹，諡武毅，祀昭忠祠，圖形紫光閣。

translations.literal: Though the emperor said Man Fu had been fooled by the enemy, he pitied his sacrifice and ordered condolence as for death in battle, the posthumous name Wuyi, enshrinement in the Shrine of Loyalty, and a portrait in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said Man Fu had been duped yet pitied his death, granted battle honors, the name Wuyi, the Shrine of Loyalty, and a place in the Hall of Purple Splendor.

sentences.zh: 豆斌，陝西固原人。

translations.literal: Dou Bin was a native of Guyuan in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Bin came from Guyuan in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 初以馬兵入提標，累遷肅州鎮標中營守備。

translations.literal: He first entered the provincial commander’s establishment as a horse soldier and was repeatedly promoted to garrison commander of the middle battalion of the Suzhou garrison standard.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a horse soldier under the provincial commander and rose to middle-battalion garrison commander at the Suzhou standard.

sentences.zh: 雍正間，從征準噶爾。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng reign he followed the campaign against the Dzungars.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng he campaigned against the Dzungars.

sentences.zh: 力戰受創，賜白金四百。

translations.literal: He fought hard, was wounded, and was granted four hundred taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: He fought fiercely, was wounded, and received four hundred taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 遷川陝督標前營游擊。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vanguard colonel of the front battalion of the Shaanxi-Gansu governor-general’s standard.
translations.idiomatic: He became vanguard colonel of the governor-general’s front battalion in Shaanxi-Gansu.

sentences.zh: 準噶爾犯科舍圖，率兵擊走之。

translations.literal: When the Dzungars attacked Kesetu, he led troops and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When the Dzungars struck Kesetu he beat them back.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，累遷提督，自廣東移廣西。

translations.literal: In the early Qianlong reign he was repeatedly promoted to provincial commander, moving from Guangdong to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianlong he became provincial commander, moving from Guangdong to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「各營鳥槍，舊式大小參差，坐臥倚伏，不能應手；

translations.literal: He memorialized: “In each camp the muskets are of the old type, large and small mixed; sitting, lying, leaning, or crouching, they cannot be handled readily;
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: “Camp muskets are old mixed sizes; whether sitting, lying, or kneeling, men cannot handle them cleanly;

sentences.zh: 又質薄易熱，難收實用。

translations.literal: they are also thin and heat easily, and hard to use effectively.
translations.idiomatic: they are thin, overheat, and fail in action.

sentences.zh: 請照陝西威字號纏絲槍式改制。

translations.literal: I ask that they be remade on the model of Shaanxi’s coiled-silk “Wei” muskets.”
translations.idiomatic: Remake them on the Shaanxi coiled-silk Wei pattern.”

sentences.zh: 」下兩廣總督議行。

translations.literal: The order was sent to the governors-general of Guangdong and Guangxi to carry out.
translations.idiomatic: The two governors-general were ordered to follow his plan.

sentences.zh: 俄，調還固原。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred back to Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent back to Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 又命以提督銜領湖北宜昌鎮總兵事。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to hold the post of commander at Yichang in Hubei with provincial commander’s rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was given provincial commander’s rank over Yichang in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 尋复歷甘肅、安西提督。

translations.literal: Soon he served again as provincial commander of Gansu and Anxi in turn.
translations.idiomatic: He then held Gansu and Anxi in succession.

sentences.zh: 命討準噶爾，帥將標兵出駐巴里坤，以輸軍馬後時，下吏議。

translations.literal: He was ordered to campaign against the Dzungars and led his standard troops to garrison Barkol; because he was late delivering army horses, he was referred to the magistrates for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered against the Dzungars, he garrisoned Barkol with his standard; late delivery of army horses brought him before the magistrates.

sentences.zh: 旋乞病，罷。

translations.literal: Soon he asked leave on grounds of illness and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He soon pleaded illness and left office.

sentences.zh: 居數月，复授安西提督，仍令赴巴里坤兆惠師。

translations.literal: After several months he was again made provincial commander of Anxi and still ordered to join Zhaohui’s army at Barkol.
translations.idiomatic: Months later he was Anxi commander again and sent to Zhaohui at Barkol.

sentences.zh: 師攻霍集占於庫車，命斌將所部從，充領隊大臣，徼巡魯克察克、闢展、庫車諸地驛路。

translations.literal: When the army attacked Khojaji at Kucha, Bin was ordered to follow with his command as column commander and to patrol the courier roads of Lukchak, Bicheng, and Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: During the siege of Khojaji at Kucha, Bin followed as column commander and patrolled the Lukchak, Bicheng, and Kucha routes.

sentences.zh: 兆惠被圍黑水，斌從副將軍富德自阿克蘇兼程赴援。

translations.literal: When Zhaohui was besieged at the Black River, Bin followed Deputy General Fude from Aksu in forced marches to relieve him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaohui was trapped at the Black River, Bin marched with Deputy General Fude from Aksu to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 師次呼爾璊，霍集占以五千人迎戰，我師分兩翼，賊據高岡，斌率中軍火器進攻。

translations.literal: The army halted at Khurun; Khojaji met them with five thousand men; our army divided into two wings; the enemy held the high ridge and Bin led the center with firearms to attack.
translations.idiomatic: At Khurun, Khojaji met them with five thousand men; the column split wings while the enemy held the heights; Bin led the center with firearms.

sentences.zh: 賊知我師馬力乏，擁眾相偪。

translations.literal: The enemy knew our horses were spent and pressed in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing our horses spent, the enemy closed in thick ranks.

sentences.zh: 阿里袞解馬至，斌偕眾將夾擊，脅中創，仍力戰，賊大敗。

translations.literal: Alihun brought up horses; Bin and the other generals struck from both sides; he was wounded in the armpit but still fought hard and the enemy was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Alihun sent remounts; Bin and the other commanders struck from both flanks; though wounded in the armpit he fought on and the enemy was shattered.

sentences.zh: 創甚遂卒，諡壯節，祀昭忠祠，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉。

translations.literal: His wounds were grave and he soon died; he was posthumously titled Zhuangjie, enshrined in the Shrine of Loyalty, and granted commandant of cavalry with cloud-rider.
translations.idiomatic: He died of his wounds, received the name Zhuangjie, the Shrine of Loyalty, and commandant of cavalry with cloud-rider.

sentences.zh: 上製詩惜之。

translations.literal: The emperor composed a poem in lament.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote a poem mourning him.

sentences.zh: 回部平，圖形紫光閣。

translations.literal: When the Muslim regions were pacified, his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: After the Muslim regions were pacified, his likeness joined the Hall of Purple Splendor.

sentences.zh: 孫{澍}，襲世職，官至山東登州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: His grandson inherited the hereditary office and rose to commander of the Dengzhou garrison in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson inherited the rank and became Dengzhou garrison commander in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 端濟布，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Duan Ji Bu, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a man of the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ji Bu of the Guwalgiya clan was a Bordered Yellow Banner Manchu.

sentences.zh: 自前鋒累遷頭等侍衛、鑲黃旗察哈爾總管。

translations.literal: From vanguard he was repeatedly promoted to first-rank bodyguard and Chahar commander of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: From vanguard he rose to first-rank bodyguard and Chahar commander of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十二年，上令選兵千佐定邊將軍兆惠出西路。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Qianlong the emperor ordered a thousand picked troops to assist Deputy Pacification General Zhaohui on the western route.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 22 the emperor chose a thousand men to reinforce Zhaohui on the western front.

sentences.zh: 自硃爾圖斯赴瑪納斯，獲得木齊鄂羅斯，並所部三百人、馬駝牛羊二千餘。

translations.literal: From Zhuer Tusi he went to Manas, captured Demuchi Eluosi, and with his following of three hundred men and more than two thousand horses, camels, cattle, and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhuer Tusi he marched to Manas, took Demuchi Eluosi, and with three hundred followers and over two thousand head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 扎哈沁頭人巴哈曼集叛走，端濟布偕侍衛奎瑪岱追捕，至小衛和勒津，降所部二百戶，又得掠台站賊札木布。

translations.literal: When the Zahakin chief Bahamanji rebelled and fled, Duan Ji Bu with Bodyguard Kuimadai pursued to Xiao Weihelejin, induced two hundred households to submit, and also captured the rebel Zhamubu who had plundered the courier stations.
translations.idiomatic: When Zahakin chief Bahamanji rebelled, Duan Ji Bu and Bodyguard Kuimadai chased him to Xiao Weihelejin, won two hundred households, and seized station-raider Zhamubu.

sentences.zh: 師捕治厄魯特頭人噶爾藏多爾濟、扎那噶爾布等，布魯古特台吉琿齊、呼爾璊台吉達瓦斬扎那噶爾布，詣端濟布軍請降。

translations.literal: When the army was suppressing the Olot chiefs Gierzang Duoerji, Zanagarbu, and others, the Burut prince Hunchi and the Khurun prince Dawa slew Zanagarbu and came to Duan Ji Bu’s army to ask surrender.
translations.idiomatic: During the suppression of Olot chiefs Gierzang Duoerji and Zanagarbu, Burut Prince Hunchi and Khurun Prince Dawa killed Zanagarbu and came to Duan Ji Bu to surrender.

sentences.zh: 端濟布遽引師還，琿齊、達瓦复叛去。

translations.literal: Duan Ji Bu abruptly led the army back; Hunchi and Dawa rebelled and fled again.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ji Bu withdrew at once; Hunchi and Dawa soon rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 上懲端濟布惟事姑息，命靖逆將軍雅爾哈善按治。

translations.literal: The emperor punished Duan Ji Bu for indulgence alone and ordered Pacification General Yarghasan to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor blamed his indulgence and ordered Pacification General Yarghasan to try the case.

sentences.zh: 師至羅克倫孟古圖嶺，獲噶爾藏多爾濟宰桑羅卜札尼瑪、得木齊敦多克，檻送巴里坤。

translations.literal: When the army reached Luokelun Menggutu Ridge they captured Gierzang Duoerji’s zaisang Luobuzhanima and Demuchi Dunduoke and sent them in cages to Barkol.
translations.idiomatic: At Luokelun Menggutu Ridge they took Gierzang Duoerji’s zaisang Luobuzhanima and Demuchi Dunduoke in cages to Barkol.

sentences.zh: 上聞，命貸端濟布罪。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this he ordered Duan Ji Bu’s crime forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: On the report the emperor pardoned Duan Ji Bu.

sentences.zh: 扎哈沁得木齊哈勒拜等謀掠台站，參贊大臣哈寧阿檄端濟布往捕，至瑪納斯，得間諜十餘。

translations.literal: When the Zahakin demuchi Halebai and others plotted to plunder the stations, Consulting Commissioner Haning’a summoned Duan Ji Bu to capture them; at Manas more than ten spies were taken.
translations.idiomatic: When Zahakin demuchi Halebai plotted against the posts, Consulting Commissioner Haning’a called Duan Ji Bu; at Manas he seized more than ten spies.

sentences.zh: 渡河至美羅託山，賊遁，收其游牧牲畜。

translations.literal: Crossing the river to Meituoshan, the enemy fled and their pastoral livestock was seized.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed to Meituoshan; the enemy fled and their herds were taken.

sentences.zh: 師圍庫車，端濟布將吉林、厄魯特兵以從。

translations.literal: When the army besieged Kucha, Duan Ji Bu followed with Jilin and Olot troops.
translations.idiomatic: At the siege of Kucha he followed with Jilin and Olot troops.

sentences.zh: 霍集占將三千人自賽里木來援，屯高阜。

translations.literal: Khojaji brought three thousand men from Sayram to relieve the city and camped on the high ground.
translations.idiomatic: Khojaji marched three thousand men from Sayram to relieve the town and camped on the heights.

sentences.zh: 端濟布偕侍衛順德納等奮擊，斬二千餘級。

translations.literal: Duan Ji Bu with Bodyguard Shunden’a and others fought fiercely and beheaded more than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ji Bu and Bodyguard Shunden’a charged and cut down more than two thousand.

sentences.zh: 師攻葉爾羌，霍集占築台城東北。

translations.literal: When the army attacked Yarkand, Khojaji built a fort northeast of the city.
translations.idiomatic: At Yarkand, Khojaji built a fort northeast of the walls.

sentences.zh: 端濟布及侍衛諾爾本將右翼後隊攻之，賊拒戰，复斬二千餘級。

translations.literal: Duan Ji Bu and Bodyguard Nuo Er Ben led the right rear to attack; the enemy resisted and more than two thousand were beheaded again.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ji Bu and Bodyguard Nuo Er Ben led the right rear; the enemy stood and another two thousand fell.

sentences.zh: 兆惠被圍於黑水，端濟布從定邊左副將軍富德赴援，十餘戰，至呼爾璊，與兆惠軍會，賜三等輕車都尉世職，授鑲紅旗滿洲副都統。

translations.literal: When Zhaohui was besieged at the Black River, Duan Ji Bu followed Left Deputy Pacification General Fude to the relief; after more than ten battles they reached Khurun, joined Zhaohui’s army, and he was granted the hereditary office of third-class commandant of light chariots and made Manchu deputy lieutenant-general of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaohui was trapped at the Black River, Duan Ji Bu followed Fude through more than ten fights to Khurun, linked with Zhaohui, and received a hereditary third-class commandant of light chariots and the Bordered Red deputy lieutenant-generalship.

sentences.zh: 師逐賊，戰於阿爾楚爾，再戰於伊西洱庫爾淖爾，端濟布將二百人截賊逃路。

translations.literal: Pursuing the enemy, they fought at Aertuxur and again at Yixi’erku’er Lake; Duan Ji Bu with two hundred men cut off the enemy’s escape route.
translations.idiomatic: In pursuit they fought at Aertuxur and again at Yixi’erku’er Lake; Duan Ji Bu with two hundred men blocked the retreat.

sentences.zh: 偵山有賊寨，越嶺攻之，被創，賜號塔什巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Scouts reported a rebel stockade in the mountains; he crossed the ridge to attack and was wounded, and was granted the title Tash Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of a mountain stronghold, he crossed the ridge, was wounded, and received the name Tash Batulu.

sentences.zh: 師還，圖形紫光閣，列前五十功臣。

translations.literal: When the army returned, his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor among the first fifty meritorious subjects.
translations.idiomatic: On the army’s return his likeness stood in the Hall of Purple Splendor among the first fifty honorees.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈都統，諡壯節，祀昭忠祠。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made lieutenant-general, titled Zhuangjie, and enshrined in the Shrine of Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously he was made lieutenant-general, named Zhuangjie, and honored in the Shrine of Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 諭以「端濟布力戰受傷，與陣亡者無異也」。

translations.literal: An edict said: “Duan Ji Bu fought hard and was wounded—no different from those who fell in battle.”
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: “Duan Ji Bu fought until he was wounded—no different from the men who died in the ranks.”

sentences.zh: 諾爾本，吳機格忒氏，滿洲正藍旗人。

translations.literal: Nuo Er Ben, of the Wujigete clan, was a man of the Manchu Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Nuo Er Ben of the Wujigete clan was a Plain Blue Banner Manchu.

sentences.zh: 以前鋒從軍。

translations.literal: He followed the army as a vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the campaign as a vanguard.

sentences.zh: 富德獲宰桑烏巴什，遣諾爾本送兆惠軍。

translations.literal: Fude captured the zaisang Ubashi and sent Nuo Er Ben to deliver him to Zhaohui’s army.
translations.idiomatic: When Fude took the zaisang Ubashi, he sent Nuo Er Ben to escort the prisoner to Zhaohui’s camp.

sentences.zh: 道遇賊，力戰，賜號克籌巴圖魯。

translations.literal: On the road he met rebels, fought hard, and was granted the title Kechou Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels blocked the road; he fought through and was given the name Kechou Batulu.

sentences.zh: 師圍庫車，霍集占來援。

translations.literal: When the army besieged Kucha, Khojaji came to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: During the siege of Kucha, Khojaji marched to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 諾爾本偕公袞楚克，侍衛齊凌札卜、齊努渾等擊賊右翼，賊敗走，逐之六十餘裡，至鄂根河口，斬獲甚眾；

translations.literal: Nuo Er Ben together with Gonggunchuke, Bodyguards Qilingzhabu, Qinuhun, and others struck the enemy’s right wing; the enemy were defeated and fled; they pursued more than sixty li to the Egen River mouth and beheaded and captured in great numbers;
translations.idiomatic: Nuo Er Ben with Gonggunchuke, Bodyguards Qilingzhabu, Qinuhun, and others hit the enemy’s right wing; the rebels broke and ran; the pursuit ran more than sixty li to the mouth of the Egen River with heavy kills and captures;

sentences.zh: 賊逃入蘇巴什山，复偕齊努渾入山搜戮：溫詔嘉焉。

translations.literal: the enemy fled into Subashi Mountain; he again entered the mountain with Qinuhun to search and slaughter: the emperor warmly praised this in an edict.
translations.idiomatic: when the enemy took refuge in Subashi Mountain he went in again with Qinuhun to hunt them down—the emperor commended him warmly in an edict.

sentences.zh: 師攻葉爾羌，偕端濟布戰城東，敗賊。

translations.literal: When the army attacked Yarkand, he fought east of the city together with Duan Ji Bu and defeated the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: At the assault on Yarkand he fought east of the walls with Duan Ji Bu and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 師還，命在乾清門行走，賚銀帛，賜騎都尉加一云騎尉世職，圖形紫光閣。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was ordered to serve at the Gate of Heavenly Purity, was given silver and silks, granted commandant of cavalry with one added cloud-rider hereditary rank, and portrayed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he was assigned to the Gate of Heavenly Purity, rewarded with silver and silks, given commandant of cavalry with an added cloud-rider inheritance, and painted in the Hall of Purple Splendor.

sentences.zh: 擢頭等侍衛，從明瑞徵緬甸，擊賊被創。

translations.literal: He was promoted to first-rank bodyguard, followed Mingrui in the Burma campaign, attacked the enemy, and was wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Raised to first-rank bodyguard, he followed Mingrui against Burma, fought the enemy, and was wounded.

sentences.zh: 尋令將兵屯騰越。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to lead troops garrisoned at Tengyue.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon told to hold Tengyue with a garrison command.

sentences.zh: 還京，擢圍場總管，加副都統銜。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he was promoted to director of the hunting grounds and given the rank of deputy lieutenant-general.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital he became director of the hunting grounds with deputy lieutenant-general rank.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 論曰：高天喜驍勇善戰，與鄂實、三格奮鬥破陣，死事為最烈。

translations.literal: The judgment says: Gao Tianxi was brave and skilled in battle; together with E Shi and San Ge he fought fiercely to break the enemy formation; his death in service was the most resolute.
translations.idiomatic: In summary: Gao Tianxi was a fierce fighter; with E Shi and San Ge he broke enemy lines at the cost of his life—the most resolute of these deaths.

sentences.zh: 和起等倉卒為賊陷，慷慨授命。

translations.literal: He Qi and others, suddenly trapped by the enemy, gave their lives generously.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi and the rest, caught unawares by the enemy, surrendered their lives without flinching.

sentences.zh: 斌與端濟布以力戰受創，得與戰死者同其血食。

translations.literal: Bin and Duan Ji Bu, for fighting hard and being wounded, were granted the same sacrificial honors as those who died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Because Bin and Duan Ji Bu fought until they were wounded, they share the sacrificial honors of the men who fell in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 旌勇勵忠，當如是也。

translations.literal: To exalt courage and encourage loyalty should be done in this way.
translations.idiomatic: Honoring bravery and stirring loyalty ought to be done just so.
